title: The Marks on the Page
label: ch:ml-marks
canDo: I can name and place the punctuation marks Malayalam prints, and say which Malayalam pieces were doing their work before they arrived.

payoff.summary: From cold: ten marks, where each one stands, and the three jobs Malayalam had already filled.
payoff.note: NINE SPANISH POINTS BEHIND ONE MALAYALAM POINT, AND ZERO NEW HEADWORDS. ML-A1-SCR-15 derives from A1-O3-01..09 -- full stop, comma, colon, question and exclamation marks, parentheses, quotation marks, hyphen, the dialogue dash and slash. The Spanish track closed its own Puntuacion category the same way at ch424: 'eight marks the corpus printed constantly and never named.' This chapter spends no new vocabulary and opens no script debt. THE NOTE'S CLAIM WAS OPENED, NOT TRUSTED. 'Not one lesson teaches any of them' is a claim about EXISTING MATERIAL, the shape that caught me on ML-A1-TIME-09 and again on LEX-42. Six Malayalam lessons matched a punctuation grep and FIVE were the word 'command' matching 'comma'; the sixth, ML-C70-um-more:46, mentions ENGLISH's commas contrastively and teaches no Malayalam mark. The claim is true. THE MARKS WERE ALREADY ON THE PAGE, AND THAT IS THE CHAPTER. ML-C02-ninre-peru-entaanu prints a question mark IN ITS HEADWORD at sequence 130, and ML-C72-ennu prints quotation marks around its quoted sentence. The book has shown these marks since the learner's second chapter and has never named one. Each lesson opens on the place the reader has already seen its mark. THE LOAD-BEARING FACT IS CHECKABLE IN UNICODE, NOT ASSERTED: the Malayalam block U+0D00-U+0D7F contains ZERO characters of general category P. The script supplied no punctuation of its own, so every mark taught here is borrowed -- and the older answer is the danda, which SA-C60-danda already teaches in the Sanskrit track. The Noto Sans Malayalam font was checked for U+0964 and U+0965 BEFORE the danda was printed, because the generator routes it through \ml{} rather than \dv{}; both are in the cmap, and missing_character is 0. THREE MARKS LAND ON JOBS MALAYALAM HAD ALREADY FILLED, which is what the recall drills: -um on every list item does the comma's work (so a Malayalam list of that kind carries no commas at all), the question words plus the -oo ending taught at ML-C03-sukhamaano do the question mark's, and ennu does the quotation marks'. The marks are for the eye; the Malayalam pieces are the grammar and they were there first. TWO CLAIMS WERE CORRECTED IN DRAFT AGAINST THE CORPUS. shubha raathri was about to be cited as a solid compound and is written WITH A SPACE, so the hyphen lesson now says the taught compounds run together (paLLikkooTaM, thalasthaanam), that a space separates the pieces where they stay apart, and that neither way uses a hyphen. And the -oo question ending was nearly asserted unattributed: ML-C03-sukhamaano:59 teaches it outright, so it is cited. THE MALAYALAM NAMES OF THE MARKS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT GIVEN. They exist, and this book cannot source them yet -- the same call ML-S147-letter-ttha makes about stroke order, and the lesson says so in the same words rather than leaving a silent gap. VERIFICATION CAUGHT THREE THINGS BEFORE CI DID. The chapter-references ceiling rejected the first draft at 59 against 46, because every lesson opened by naming an earlier chapter NUMBER; all thirteen were rewritten to name the thing ('since you first asked anybody their name'), which is what that test's own documentation prescribes and is better teaching. The duration ceiling caught ML-W108-question-mark at 359s. And scan_latex_log_warnings.py -- new to the routine after it failed CI on chapter 107 -- caught an underfull hbox at badness 2644 that check-book-compile.sh reported as 'ok'.
